objective: To spell adjectives with the -ious and -eous suffixes
defs: easy to see or understand; clear
eager to know or learn about something
happening at exactly the same time

sentences.serious: The doctor gave the family a ____________________ look before explaining the results.
sentences.obvious: It was ____________________ from the smile on her face that she had won a prize.
sentences.curious: The ____________________ cat crept closer to the rustling leaves at the edge of the garden.
sentences.furious: The coach was ____________________ when the player knocked the ball into their own net.
sentences.glorious: The ____________________ sunshine made the whole park glow with warm golden light.
sentences.mysterious: A ____________________ package arrived at the school with no name on the label.
sentences.spontaneous: The crowd broke into ____________________ applause when the performer took a bow.
sentences.courteous: The waiter was ____________________ and brought everything we ordered with a warm smile.
sentences.simultaneous: The twins gave ____________________ answers and the class burst out laughing in surprise.
sentences.hideous: The ____________________ mask in the shop window made the small children squeal and run away.

starter.question: Can you add -ious or -eous to make adjectives from these roots?
starter.ruleBox: -ious and -eous both mean 'full of'. -eous follows roots ending in a vowel (court, hide). -ious follows most others.

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Look at the endings. Can you spot two different patterns?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words end in -ious or -eous. Both suffixes mean 'full of' or 'having that quality'. The -eous ending often follows roots of Latin or French origin ending in a vowel: hide → hideous, court → courteous.

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: taking great care; full of concern or interest

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Entered English in the 1300s from Old French curios, meaning inquisitive.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use curious to mean eager to know or learn about something.

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: The root cura also gives us cure, accurate and secure — words all connected to care and attention.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.hint: Look carefully at the letters before the -ous. Is it i or e?
wordSort.answerNote: -ious: serious, obvious, curious, furious, glorious, mysterious. -eous: spontaneous, courteous, simultaneous, hideous.

wordShed.def: strange and difficult to explain or understand
wordShed.sentence: A mysterious light appeared above the forest and then vanished without a trace.

morphMatrix.def: something strange that is difficult to explain
